solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Plant accused here (4)

blocks.note: a broad-leaved weed, not a verb about framing someone
the enclosure in a courtroom where the defendant stands

annotation.surface: A courtroom plea that the defendant was set up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb about framing someone, which chimes with 'accused'; here it is the weed DOCK, and the DOCK is also where the accused stands in a British court.
annotation.definitionFit: Two unrelated senses share the spelling: a common weed, and the courtroom enclosure for the defendant.

entries.clue: Place to sleep on river for rodent (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so DORM is written first

annotation.surface: A small creature bedding down by a riverbank.
annotation.walkthrough: The OUSE is one of several English rivers of that name, a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain case of a specific animal defined by its class: the dormouse is a small hibernating rodent.

entries.clue: Reason why Australian is in Church? (5)

indicatorNotes.is in: something that is in something else is contained by it, so AUS goes inside CE

blocks.note: AUS is the abbreviation for Australian

annotation.surface: Asking what brings an Australian into church.
annotation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is a standard crossword abbreviation for church.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the reason why something happens is its cause.

entries.clue: Place near South coast where side path collapses (8)

indicatorNotes.collapses: something that collapses loses its shape, so the letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: A coastal footpath crumbling into the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: Spithead is the stretch of water off Portsmouth, between the mainland and the Isle of Wight, long used as a naval anchorage.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: the anchorage lies just off Portsmouth on England's south coast.

entries.clue: Favour proportional representation, free to be developed (6)

indicatorNotes.to be developed: something developed is worked into a new form, so FREE is rearranged

annotation.surface: A political slogan backing a fairer voting system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like part of the political message, but it is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to favour one option is to rate it above the others.

entries.clue: Islander I’d wrongly associated with Indian art (11)

indicatorNotes.wrongly: letters put together wrongly are out of order, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Someone confessing a mistaken belief about where a craft came from.
annotation.walkthrough: Trinidad has a large population of Indian descent, so the surface is closer to the answer than it looks.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a native of the Caribbean island of Trinidad is one kind of islander.

entries.clue: After exams regularly nurse in part of capital (4,3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter of EXAMS is kept
indicatorNotes.After: the second piece is written after the first, so TEND follows EAS

annotation.surface: A nurse working in a London district once her exams are done.
annotation.walkthrough: London's East End is the traditionally working-class district east of the City.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital is London and this district is one part of it.

entries.clue: Animal’s home over time — a hollow (4)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue a piece over another sits above it, so DEN comes before T

blocks.note: a den is a wild animal's lair

annotation.surface: An animal's lair that has become just an empty hole over time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over time' reads as 'eventually'; in a down clue 'over' puts DEN above T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a small depression pressed into a surface.

entries.clue: As expected, wine unopened after heavy defeat (7)

indicatorNotes.unopened: a thing unopened has not had its front breached, so WINE loses its opening letter
indicatorNotes.after: the second piece is written after the first, so INE follows ROUT

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

annotation.surface: A beaten team, as usual, not even getting to open the wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unopened' pictures a corked bottle; in the wordplay it removes the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective sense: a routine event is ordinary, just what you expected.

entries.clue: The writer’s expert, vehement, he leaves — a change for better? (11)

indicatorNotes.leaves: when HE leaves, he departs from the word, so VEHEMENT is left without HE

annotation.surface: A writer asking whether an ardent expert's departure would be for the best.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so 'the writer's' gives I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase rather than a one-word synonym: making something better is exactly this.

entries.clue: Dramatist is brilliant, so educational — Norwegian originally (5)

indicatorNotes.originally: a word's origin is where it starts, so take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Is Brilliant So Educational Norwegian

annotation.surface: Praise for a playwright's instructive brilliance, with a nod to his nationality.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian playwright, so the last word does double duty in the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the author of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler is one dramatist among many.

entries.clue: Too strict about summary, English (11)

blocks.note: over = about, concerning (a row over money)

annotation.surface: A complaint that a teacher marked an English summary too harshly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is often a container or reversal signal; here it simply means OVER.
annotation.definitionFit: Strict here means exact, so too strict is exact to excess.

entries.clue: Chat idly about river near simple home of Wordsworth (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so GAS goes around R
indicatorNotes.near: something near another is next to it, so MERE is placed beside G(R)AS

blocks.note: mere = simple, as in a mere child

annotation.surface: Idle chatter by a river, with a simple cottage in the Lake District.
annotation.walkthrough: The poet William Wordsworth lived at Dove Cottage in Grasmere, a village in the English Lake District.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by association: the poet lived at Dove Cottage in this Lake District village and is buried there.

entries.clue: Transatlantic uncle’s performing as strong man? (6)

blocks.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA, across the Atlantic

annotation.surface: An American uncle doing a strongman act.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Samson is a strong man by legend, not by trade.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the biblical hero whose strength lay in his hair is the archetypal strong man.

entries.clue: Large religious service I have joined (7)

indicatorNotes.joined: pieces that are joined are stuck together end to end, so MASS and IVE combine

blocks.note: the Mass is the Catholic service

annotation.surface: Someone who has joined a big congregation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large' sits at the front looking like an adjective for the service, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym, the answer being the stronger word: very large indeed.

entries.clue: Farm animal’s look (6)

blocks.note: informal, as in 'take a look at this'

annotation.surface: Describing a farm animal's expression.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but means 'is', linking the two definitions; 'have a gander' is British slang for having a look.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses share the word: the male goose, and a quick look in informal British speech.

entries.clue: Artist and doctor on initially leisurely evening stroll (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so take the first letters of leisurely and evening
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue a piece on another sits above it, so RA MB comes first

annotation.surface: A painter and a doctor out for a gentle evening walk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leisurely evening stroll' reads as one phrase, but only 'stroll' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: both mean an unhurried walk for pleasure.

entries.clue: Mischief an ensign has at sea? (11)

indicatorNotes.at sea: to be at sea is to be confused, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A junior naval officer getting up to pranks on a voyage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the naval ensign so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though the answer is plural and informal: high-spirited trickery.

entries.clue: Girl welcomes Italian friendship (5)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: a host who welcomes a guest takes them inside, so AMY takes IT in

annotation.surface: A girl warmly receiving an Italian visitor as a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: The girl is AMY, one of the short names setters lean on; IT for Italian is standard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the answer being the more formal word, used of peaceful relations between nations.

entries.clue: Having power for day, leave out this rugby forward (4)

indicatorNotes.for: one thing given for another replaces it, so P stands in place of D

blocks.note: to drop is to leave out

annotation.surface: A coach dropping a forward in favour of a more powerful one.
annotation.walkthrough: In rugby the props are the two forwards on either side of the front row of the scrum.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this front-row position is one of the eight forward positions in rugby union.

entries.clue: Bring up commendation, initially ignored (5)

indicatorNotes.initially ignored: the letter at the start is ignored, so PRAISE loses its P

annotation.surface: A child's good deed going unpraised at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' works both for a child and for a subject in conversation.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym that covers both rearing a child and mentioning a topic.

entries.clue: Heat source from brazier, if nobody about? (7)

indicatorNotes.from: taken from inside the words, so the letters sit within the phrase
indicatorNotes.about: turned about means turned round, so the letters read backwards

annotation.surface: Warmth from a brazier when there's no one around to use it.
annotation.walkthrough: A brazier is itself a heat source, which makes it look like the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a large outdoor fire is one source of heat among many.

entries.clue: More attractive before — not drinking. That is right (8)

annotation.surface: Someone claiming they looked better before they gave up drink.
annotation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) means abstaining from alcohol.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain comparative synonym; both are comparatives, so they swap cleanly.

entries.clue: It flows in city — Newcastle (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies in the words, spread across city and Newcastle

annotation.surface: A river running through the city of Newcastle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: the Tyne runs through Newcastle upon Tyne.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-style definition by function: a river is something that flows.
